note: Rebuilt from the option tape over 800 days, not replayed on chains the agent recorded, and priced at a modelled relative spread of 0.041 per leg. That is the median across the two sided legs of the 1 September chain. It is deliberately not the 0.1280 the live calibration wrote, because that median is taken over a population in which 26 of 122 legs were quoted one sided and compute to a relative spread of 2.0; a leg nobody is bidding on is untradeable, not expensive. Read the two arms together. Trading every session loses money net of cost, at a net Sharpe of -1.94. Selecting sessions is the whole difference, and even then gross 1.93 falls to net 0.40, so execution cost takes about four fifths of the gross result. The classified arm is an out of sample fitted model choosing its sessions, and no fitted model ships in this agent: neither of the two bars in convex/classifier.py was cleared, so the live path decides on a documented volatility regime rule instead. This arm is therefore what the structures are worth if selection works, not a forecast of what the agent will do. Sharpe over 509 sessions is arithmetic, not evidence, and the strangle arm rests on four trades, which is why its ratio prints as a dot rather than a number.
